conventions: בְּעֵינֵי + suffix rendered by an English verb of seeming or thinking — v.3 בְּעֵינֶיךָ → *Thinkest*, v.13 בְּעֵינָיו → *seemeth* — gives that verb to the fused preposition and construct noun (rules 30, 40), headed on עַיִן, while the suffix keeps the pronoun the ASV writes for it (*thou*, *him*) and the predicate adjective keeps its own word (*good*). The competing reading, the verb as a copula on the adjective with בְּ and עַיִן unrepresented, was considered and not taken.

עָרַךְ in this chapter is the light-verb *put/set ... in array*, headed on *array* (rule 44). An object the ASV supplies where the Hebrew writes none is `added` and not the verb's — v.10 *them*, v.17 *the battle* in the first clause — while the written מִלְחָמָה takes *the battle* with a supplied *the* (vv. 9, 17 second clause). v.11's *themselves* is coreferential with the subject and stays with the verb as the ASV's intransitive rendering; competing reading *themselves* added is named in the note.
report: Checked all 42 candidate lemmas. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by what the ASV wrote: waw takes And/So/Then/But/that/who/with or the *And when*/*Now when*/*So when* pair, and every apodosis waw after such a pair (vv. 6, 8, 10, 15, 16, 17, 19) is unrepresented; dative לְ is bare before *David*/*them*/*me* (vv. 5, 6, 7, 12, 17) and takes *to*/*unto* only where written (vv. 3, 7, 14); the assimilated article takes *the* where the ASV writes one (vv. 4, 9, 14) and nothing where it writes *to battle* (v. 7).

The added units were read together since the candidate table cannot see them: v.5 *certain persons* (supplied subject) and *were served* (supplied lexical verb), v.5 *then* beside a waw already holding *and*, v.8 *of it*, v.10 *them* and v.17 *the battle* (supplied objects of עָרַךְ), v.18 *the men of*. v.11's *themselves* stays with עָרַךְ as the intransitive/reflexive rendering, which differs from v.10's *them* (a distinct referent) on the terms rule 44 draws; not a split.
The בְּעֵינֵי idiom is treated one way in both places it occurs (v.3 *Thinkest*, v.13 *seemeth* on the fused preposition and noun, suffix keeping its pronoun); recorded as a convention.

One defensible alternative not patched: v.16 לִפְנֵיהֶם → *at their head* is fused as one לְ+פָּנֶה unit; rule 30's *to meet* example would support splitting *at* to לְ and *head* to פָּנֶה. The verse note names a competing reading and the unit's information content is the same either way, so it was left as accepted.
BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences (bare dative לְ and בַּעֲבוּר, apodosis waws, object markers). None is a genuine error.
No promotion or amendment: nothing here generalises beyond what rules 14, 40, 44, 45 and 55 already say.
